subsystem: Platform: monorepo, build, config, CLI, Docker, CI, test strategy, and the master phase plan
summary: This is the scaffolding the other seven subsystems stand on, plus the one ordered delivery sequence that reconciles their phases. The single idea that makes it leaner than mcphub: there is exactly one of everything. One database (Postgres 16 + pgvector), one migration chain (drizzle files covering our tables AND better-auth's generated ones), one config schema that fails fast at boot, one build tool per artifact kind (tsc for Node, vite for the SPA, nothing else), one Docker image with no INSTALL_EXT variant, one npm package (the CLI), one test runner. mcphub carries two storage backends × two DAO switches × three catalogs × five auth stacks × two era transports, and pays for it with a Dockerfile that installs Rust and Docker-in-Docker, a CI file whose build and integration jobs are commented out (.github/workflows/ci.yml:48-113), and coverage thresholds set to zero (jest.config.cjs:31-38). We delete the variants instead of testing them. The two gates that are non-negotiable and that mcphub does not have: `pnpm build` runs on every PR, and an end-to-end test drives a real `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` client through the built gateway into a real upstream MCP server.
phase:
MASTER PHASE PLAN — one ordered sequence, reconciling all eight subsystem designs. Each phase ships a usable vertical slice. Sizes are dev-weeks for one strong full-stack dev.

P0 SKELETON THAT BOOTS — 1.0w — deps: none — owner: platform (me).
Scope: pnpm workspace + 4 packages + `tsc -b` project references; zod config schema with fail-fast exit 78; drizzle schema stub + migration runner under a pg advisory lock; Dockerfile + docker-compose with pgvector health-gated; pino logger with request-id; `/health/live|ready`; `/metrics`; vitest + testcontainers harness; CI with every gate already at its FINAL numbers (they pass trivially because there is no code — this is deliberate, gates never get "turned on later", which is exactly how mcphub's jobs ended up commented out).
Demo: `docker compose up` → ready in <15s; `curl /health/ready` 200; unset AUTH_SECRET → process exits 78 printing `AUTH_SECRET: must be at least 32 characters — run \`mcprouter secret\`` and nothing else; CI green on an empty PR.

P1 ONE TOOL, END TO END — 2.0w — deps: P0 — owners: core engine + HTTP edge + auth.
Scope: core upstream registry (generation counter + `connectStillWanted` guard, mcphub mcpService.ts:832/:2035), stdio + streamable-http + SSE upstream clients, SSRF guard with per-redirect validation (mcphub :1382-1396), tool cache namespaced `<server><sep><tool>` at cache time (:638); server: legacy-era (2025-11-25) Streamable HTTP `POST /mcp`, 405 on GET/DELETE (we never ship the standalone stream, so this is free); better-auth core + apiKey plugin wired as configuration, not code.
Demo: `mcprouter servers add` an npx-launched filesystem server, create a key, point Claude Code at `https://hub/mcp` with that bearer key, list and call a tool. A real client through a real upstream on day 21.

P2 SCOPE AND THE VISIBILITY INVARIANT — 1.5w — deps: P1 — owners: auth/authz + core.
Scope: Group = membership + per-server item selection in one record (mcphub entities/Group.ts:23-33 — this shape is right, keep it); per-server tool enable/disable enforced at CALL time not only list time (their CVE fix afcc72f); identical error text for hidden and nonexistent (their ToolUnavailableError :2654); key↔group full-containment scoping (GHSA-454m-4vm6-842f, sseService.ts:228-302); audit rows written per call.
Demo: two keys, two groups. Key A lists 4 tools, key B lists 2. Calling a key-A-only tool with key B returns a response byte-identical to calling a tool that was never defined. This is the phase where the security tests hit their 90% per-glob gate.

P3 THE OPERATOR UI — 2.5w — deps: P2 (needs the REST surface + auth) — owner: web. CAN RUN IN PARALLEL with P4 if a second dev exists; this is the natural fork point.
Scope: vite + React 19 + Tailwind v4 `@theme` token block + shadcn/ui properly installed + TanStack Query + cmdk palette; servers grid with live status dots, server form, groups, keys, users, log stream, keyboard-first navigation.
Demo: an operator who has never seen the CLI adds a server, builds a group, issues a scoped key and copies a client config block — entirely in the browser, dark, dense, no page over 1.5s to interactive.

P4 OBSERVABILITY FOR REAL — 1.0w — deps: P1 (instrument as you build; this phase lands the surfaces) — owner: observability.
Scope: prom-client histograms per server/tool/outcome; OTel sdk-node started only when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set; pino JSON + pino-roll file sink; request-id propagated client→hub→upstream; persisted activity log with retention job; `/api/health` deep view; per-server latency sparkline in the UI.
Demo: a Grafana panel of p95 tool latency per upstream, and one distributed trace spanning client → hub → upstream. mcphub's own docs admit they have none of this and punt to an external APM.

P5 CONTEXT COST + SMART ROUTING — 2.0w — deps: P2 (scope resolution) and P0 (pgvector) — owner: routing/cost.
Scope: cl100k token counting over the exact projected payload; per-server and per-group gross vs exposed; `$smart` meta-tools with progressive disclosure; pgvector cosine search with the scope predicate pushed INTO the SQL (never filter after LIMIT); embedding sync skipped by tool-set hash; hash-fallback embeddings when no API key so the feature works with zero configuration.
Demo: a 14-server group costing 61k tokens of tool definitions drops to 1.2k under `$smart`, the UI shows both numbers side by side, and `search_tools` still finds the right tool. A scoped search over a 1000-row fixture returns zero out-of-scope rows at LIMIT 5 — the regression test that proves the SQL-side filter.

P6 MARKETPLACE AND INSTALL — 1.0w — deps: P3 — owner: catalog.
Scope: registry.modelcontextprotocol.io proxy WITH caching (mcphub re-parses a 2.4 MB servers.json on every call, marketService.ts:12-34); install flow writes a server config; MCPB upload with traversal-hardened name and atomic rename (their mcpbController.ts:97-166 is correct, reproduce it).
Demo: search the registry from the cmdk palette, press enter, the server is connected and its tools are listed 10 seconds later.

P7 HARDENING AND 1.0 — 1.5w — deps: all — owners: all.
Scope: secrets encrypted at rest — upstream OAuth tokens, env and headers, AES-256-GCM with AAD (mcphub stores all three in plaintext: oauthSettingsStore.ts:107-129, config/index.ts:150-252 — this is our headline differentiator, not a corner-cut); upstream OAuth client with RFC 9728 discovery + RFC 8707 `resource` on both authorize and token; MCPRouter-as-AS via the better-auth `mcp` plugin with DCR left OFF; rate limits via the apiKey plugin; accessibility pass (roles, focus traps, no emoji-as-UI); docs; e2e against the released image; multi-arch signed release.
Demo: `docker run ghcr.io/…/mcprouter:1.0.0`, a team of five operators, three clients, and `pg_dump | grep -c 'sk-'` returns 0.

TOTAL: 12.5 dev-weeks of scope. Honest calendar: ~4 months for one dev (12.5w + ~30% for SDK quirks, misbehaving upstream servers, and review), or ~10 weeks for two devs forking at P3 (web) / P4-P5 (backend). Anyone promising a 1.0 in six weeks is planning to delete a gate.

NOT IN THIS PLAN: P8 MODERN ERA (2026-07-28). Trigger: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` ships `LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = '2026-07-28'`. Size: 1.0w IF P1 held the line — a new handler in `packages/server/src/mcp/modern.ts` beside `legacy.ts`, MRTR `InputRequiredResult` plumbing, `subscriptions/listen`, `-32020`/`-32022`, and deleting the session map. It becomes a 6-week rewrite if session identity ever leaks into `packages/core`, which is why the tsconfig project reference and the core package.json (no hono, no better-auth) mechanically forbid it from P0 onward.

decisions.decision: Four packages, one solution tsconfig, TypeScript project references. `core` (MCP engine + drizzle schema + migrations, deps: sdk/zod/drizzle/pino/pg — NO hono, NO better-auth) ← `server` (hono + better-auth + HTTP/MCP edge) ; `web` (vite SPA, no TS dep on either) ; `cli` (type-only import of core, zero runtime workspace deps). Dependency direction is one-way and enforced twice: by `references` in tsconfig, and by pnpm's isolated node_modules, which makes `import { Hono } from 'hono'` inside core fail to resolve rather than fail review.
decisions.rationale: The binding constraint from the spec facts is that session identity must never enter `packages/core`. A prose rule gets violated in month three. A package boundary that cannot resolve the import gets violated never. This is also what makes the future modern-era handler a new file instead of an engine rewrite.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub is one package. `src/services/mcpService.ts` is 5006 lines and holds engine, transport, session and HTTP concerns together, which is exactly why `enableSessionRebuild` had to rehydrate private SDK internals (sseService.ts:105) — there was no seam to put the era behind. We spend 48 lines of tsconfig to buy that seam.

decisions.decision: Build with `tsc -b` and nothing else for core/server/cli; `vite build` for web. No tsup, no unbuild, no esbuild script. `verbatimModuleSyntax: true`, `module: nodenext`, explicit `.js` in relative imports.
decisions.rationale: Ladder rung 3/4. We ship a Docker image, not a library — nobody tree-shakes our server, so bundling buys zero and costs a config file, a sourcemap hop and a class of 'works in dev, breaks in the bundle' ESM bugs. `tsc -b` gives real incremental builds and `--watch` for free. `verbatimModuleSyntax` is load-bearing beyond style: it guarantees the CLI's `import type` of core erases, so the published CLI genuinely has zero runtime dependencies.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub also uses plain tsc, and that part is right — but their `verify-dist.js` never runs in CI because the build job is commented out (ci.yml:48-113), so the thing tsc produces is unverified on every PR. We keep their tool and add the gate they removed.

decisions.decision: Distribution is split by audience. The hub ships ONLY as a multi-arch Docker image on GHCR. The CLI ships ONLY as an npm package named `mcprouter` (~60 KB, zero runtime deps, `node:util.parseArgs` + global fetch). An unknown subcommand prints usage and exits 1. There is no `serve` fall-through.
decisions.rationale: The product requires Postgres 16 + pgvector, so `npx mcprouter` without a database was never going to work — pretending otherwise just adds a code path. Splitting means the thing an operator installs on their laptop is 60 KB and installs in two seconds, while the thing that runs in prod is a pinned image.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub's `bin/cli.js:13-29` routes known subcommands to the CLI and falls through to the SERVER BOOTSTRAP for everything else. Reject it: a typo (`mcphub sever list`) boots a production server that runs migrations as a side effect, `--help` is ambiguous about which program is answering, and it welds the client package to the server package so the CLI can never be small. One `if` and an exit code buys all of that back.

decisions.decision: One zod schema for all env vars, parsed once at boot in `packages/server/src/config.ts`, composed from a `CoreConfigSchema` that `packages/core` exports for its own vars. On failure, print EVERY issue as `VAR: message` plus a remediation hint, print no values, and `process.exit(78)` (EX_CONFIG). `AUTH_SECRET`, `DATABASE_URL` and `PUBLIC_URL` are REQUIRED with no fallback. Every secret also accepts `<VAR>_FILE` pointing at a mounted file. The config object carries a `toJSON` that redacts secrets so a stray `logger.info({config})` cannot leak them.
decisions.rationale: Boot-time validation is a trust boundary and the doctrine's explicit carve-out. Exit 78 rather than 1 so an orchestrator's restart policy can distinguish 'this will never work' from 'transient'. `_FILE` is six lines and is how Docker `secrets:` and Kubernetes projected volumes actually deliver secrets. `PUBLIC_URL` must be required, not inferred from the Host header, because RFC 8707 token audiences and RFC 9728 resource identifiers are validated against it — inferring it from a request header is host-header injection straight into the audience claim.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub generates a random JWT secret per process when JWT_SECRET is unset (config/jwt.ts:4-14). That is silent, and it breaks the moment you run two replicas: replica B rejects every token replica A issued, intermittently, with no log line explaining it. Our failure is a hard stop with the exact fix command in the message. mcphub also stores `env`/`headers` as plaintext and expands `${VAR}` at connect time (config/index.ts:150-252) with no boot-time check that the referenced var exists — we validate placeholders at save time, not at 3am.

decisions.decision: Real drizzle migration files in `packages/core/drizzle/`, applied in-process at boot, wrapped in `pg_advisory_lock` so concurrent replicas serialize. better-auth's tables are generated into `packages/core/src/db/auth-schema.ts` via `@better-auth/cli generate` and re-exported from the schema barrel, so drizzle-kit sees them and ONE migration chain covers the whole database. CI runs `drizzle-kit generate` and fails on `git diff --exit-code drizzle/`.
decisions.rationale: The advisory lock is three lines and removes the entire class of 'two pods raced the same DDL' incidents. Folding better-auth into our chain means one `pnpm db:migrate`, one rollback story, and one `pg_dump` that restores to a working system. The CI diff check is the cheapest possible answer to 'someone edited schema.ts and forgot the migration' — it catches it on the PR, not on the deploy.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub uses `synchronize: true` (db/connection.ts:92) — no migrations at all — except `vector_embeddings`, which is `synchronize: false` with hand-written DDL and ALTERs (:217-263), while better-auth runs a SEPARATE kysely migration system. Three schema-management strategies in one database. Their own AGENTS.md admits adding one persisted field touches seven layers. Ours touches one file plus a generated migration.

decisions.decision: Base image `node:22-bookworm-slim`, with `uv`/`uvx` copied as static binaries from `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv` and one managed CPython baked in at build time (`uv python install 3.13`). Add `git` and `ca-certificates`. Nothing else. Non-root `USER node`. No INSTALL_EXT variant, no Rust, no Docker-in-Docker, no Playwright, no procps. Target ≤400 MB uncompressed, amd64 + arm64.
decisions.rationale: mcphub is right that the image must run both `npx` and `uvx` — that requirement is real and they paid to learn it. They are wrong about the direction: `uv` is a static Rust binary that needs no Python installation and fetches its own interpreter, so you can add uvx to a Node base far more cheaply than you can add Node to a Python base. Baking the interpreter at build time keeps first-run latency and egress-restricted deploys working. procps disappears because we kill stdio children by process group (`process.kill(-pid)` on a detached spawn) instead of pulling in tree-kill.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub uses `python:3.13-slim-trixie` + hand-installed Node 22 + procps (Dockerfile:7-14), and INSTALL_EXT=true adds Rust, a Docker Engine daemon and amd64-only Playwright — which is why their full variant is multi-GB and cannot be cleanly multi-arch. Dropping DinD is also a security decision: hosting MCP servers via a privileged inner Docker daemon is a container-escape surface. Run those as sibling containers and add them as streamable-http upstreams. We DO copy their CMD lesson verbatim: the runtime stage has no pnpm and no corepack, CMD is `node dist/index.js`, because corepack re-download breaks non-root and egress-restricted runs (their Dockerfile:67-71).

decisions.decision: Three health surfaces with different audiences. `GET /health/live` — unauthenticated, no DB, always 200 unless the event loop is wedged. `GET /health/ready` — unauthenticated, 200 only if the DB answers and migrations are applied, 503 otherwise, body is one status word with no error strings. `GET /api/health` — authenticated, the full picture including per-upstream state. Upstream MCP server health is deliberately NOT in the readiness probe.
decisions.rationale: A dead upstream must not pull the hub out of the load balancer — the hub is still correctly serving every other server and correctly reporting the failure. Conflating them means one flaky third-party MCP server can take down your whole gateway. The unauthenticated probes leak nothing: a Postgres connection error string in a public 503 body tells an attacker your DB host, port and version.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub's `GET /health` is unauthenticated, returns 503 on DB failure but returns 200 with body "degraded" when servers are down (healthController.ts:32-46) — so a naive `httpGet 200` probe passes a hub whose upstreams are all dead. Our split makes the probe honest in both directions.

decisions.decision: `packages/web` builds to `dist/` with vite `base: './'`; `packages/server` serves it with `serveStatic` from `@hono/node-server`, mounted LAST, behind a catch-all that explicitly excludes `/api`, `/mcp`, `/health`, `/metrics` and `/.well-known`. `assets/*` gets `immutable, max-age=31536000` (vite hashes the filenames), `index.html` gets `no-store`. Subpath deployment comes free from `new URL(PUBLIC_URL).pathname` fed to `app.basePath()`. Dev uses vite's proxy — no CORS code anywhere.
decisions.rationale: Ladder rung 5: the installed dependency already does static serving with range requests and etags. The exclusion list is an allowlist inversion done deliberately: a new API prefix that someone forgets to exclude serves index.html and produces a confusing 200-with-HTML instead of a 404, so the list lives next to the route registration with a comment. Subpath support costs two lines because we already require PUBLIC_URL for OAuth.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub threads a separate `config.basePath` through the whole app and mounts every route family under it (server.ts:141-168). We derive it from the URL we already have to require, so there is no second source of truth about where the hub lives — and no way for the OAuth redirect URI and the asset base to disagree.

decisions.decision: vitest 5, not jest. Three layers with distinct file suffixes: `*.test.ts` (unit, no I/O, colocated with source), `*.itest.ts` (integration, real Postgres via `@testcontainers/postgresql` running the EXACT `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` image production uses), `test/e2e/*.e2e.ts` (a real SDK `Client` against the built server and a real fixture upstream). `retry: 0` in CI — a flaky test is deleted, not retried.
decisions.rationale: Our whole stack is Node ESM and the SDK is ESM-first. vitest transforms with esbuild natively; jest needs ts-jest plus `--experimental-vm-modules` and still fights ESM mocking. We already have vite for the web package, so vitest is zero marginal dependency and the web tests share one config. Using the identical pgvector image in tests and prod matters specifically because HNSW index behaviour and operator availability differ by pgvector build.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub runs Jest + ts-jest ESM over 209 files, and `tests/setup.ts` forces `DB_URL=sqlite::memory:` while their Postgres integration job is disabled — so DB mode, pgvector smart routing and activity logging are only ever exercised against a database they do not ship. Their runner choice cascaded into testing the wrong database. That is the failure we are buying out of.

decisions.decision: Every PR runs: frozen-lockfile install → oxlint + prettier --check → `pnpm build` (tsc -b + vite build) → unit → integration (testcontainers) → e2e (real SDK client through the built server) → `drizzle-kit generate` + `git diff --exit-code drizzle/` → amd64-only Docker build (no push). Coverage gates: global lines 70 / functions 70 / branches 60, plus hard per-glob gates of lines 90 / branches 85 on `packages/core/src/security/**` and `packages/core/src/tools/**`, and 85/75 on `packages/server/src/mcp/**`. Hard 8-minute timeout on the e2e job. Any PR that edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to skip or disable a job requires a second approval via CODEOWNERS.
decisions.rationale: A uniform 90% gate makes people write tests for glue code and then quietly lower the gate. A modest global floor plus a ruthless gate on exactly the modules where CVEs actually occurred (tool visibility, SSRF, scope resolution) puts the effort where the bugs are. The CODEOWNERS rule exists because the historically observed failure mode is not 'the gate was never set' — it is 'the gate was set, it got slow, and someone commented it out'.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub's ci.yml runs lint, tsc and jest with Codecov, but the build and integration-test jobs are entirely commented out (ci.yml:48-113) so `pnpm build` and `verify-dist.js` never execute on a PR, and all four coverage thresholds are 0 (jest.config.cjs:31-38). They also have no e2e against a built image at all. Every gate we set is one they have and disabled, plus the e2e they never had.

decisions.decision: Supply chain: all GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs, workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`, `pull_request` (never `pull_request_target`) so PR jobs hold no secrets, PR Docker builds never push. Releases are tag-driven: buildx multi-arch push to GHCR with `--provenance --sbom`, cosign keyless signing via GitHub OIDC, and `npm publish --provenance` for the CLI. No changesets.
decisions.rationale: Pinned SHAs and no-secrets-on-PR are the two controls that actually stop the common compromised-action attack; everything else in this area is theatre. Provenance, SBOM and cosign are literally three flags on tools we are already running, so the ladder says take them. Changesets is a whole workflow ceremony for exactly one published package — the git tag is the version.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub's release is tag-driven multi-arch to Docker Hub plus npm plus a GitHub release and a bilingual release-notes validator — more machinery than we need, and no signing, SBOM or provenance on any of it.

decisions.decision: Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM: stop accepting new connections, let in-flight tool calls finish up to `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 10s), SIGTERM then SIGKILL every stdio child's process GROUP, close the pool, exit 0. And an honest documented ceiling: because v1 serves the legacy era, downstream session state lives in `packages/server` memory, so multi-replica deployments need session affinity on `/mcp`. Everything else — required AUTH_SECRET, advisory-locked migrations, no in-memory config — is already replica-safe.
decisions.rationale: Killing the process group rather than the pid is what prevents orphaned `npx`/`uvx` grandchildren accumulating until the container OOMs, and it is stdlib (`spawn(..., {detached:true})` + `process.kill(-pid)`), which is how we delete the tree-kill dependency and therefore procps from the image. Stating the affinity requirement out loud is the point: it is transitional debt that the 2026-07-28 spec deletes for us, so we document it rather than build a Redis-backed session store we will throw away.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub attacks the same problem from the wrong end with `enableSessionRebuild`, which rehydrates private SDK internals to survive restarts (sseService.ts:105) — brittle across every SDK version bump, in service of a concept the spec is removing. We write one paragraph of documentation instead of a subsystem.

interfaces.name: Env
interfaces.notes: EMBEDDING_PROVIDER='none' keeps Smart Routing usable with zero configuration via a deterministic hash embedding — mcphub's 100-dim fallback (vectorSearchService.ts:1029) is a good idea, reproduced. No BASE_PATH var: the subpath comes from PUBLIC_URL's pathname.

interfaces.name: loadConfig
interfaces.notes: Tested directly: one unit test per required var asserts exit code 78 and that the message names the var. `loadConfig(fakeEnv)` takes an injected env so the tests need no process mutation.

interfaces.name: runMigrations
interfaces.notes: Integration test: two concurrent runMigrations() against a fresh container both succeed and the migration table has one row per file. This is the whole multi-replica DDL story — 40 lines instead of a leader-election sidecar.

interfaces.name: health + static routes
interfaces.notes: If WEB_DIST does not exist the static mounts are skipped and the server logs `UI not built — API only`. That is the dev-without-vite-build case and the API-only deployment case, one branch covering both.

interfaces.name: mcprouter (CLI)
interfaces.sketch:
mcprouter <command> [args]           # node:util.parseArgs, global fetch, ZERO runtime deps

  login [--url URL] [--key KEY]      # prompts for the key if not given; verifies with GET /api/me
  logout
  servers  ls | add <file.json|-> | rm <name> | toggle <name> [--on|--off] | logs <name>
  groups   ls | add <name> | rm <name> | add-server <group> <server> | rm-server <group> <server>
  tools    ls [--group G] [--server S]
  call     <tool> [k=v ...] [--params-json JSON] [--group G]   # the debugging workhorse
  keys     ls | create <name> [--group G] [--expires 30d] | rm <id>
  doctor                            # GET /api/health — DB, migration id, embedding dim, per-upstream state
  secret                            # prints crypto.randomBytes(48).toString('base64'). AUTH_SECRET is required,
                                    # so the tool that makes one is one command away.

Auth  : Authorization: Bearer <api key>. ONE scheme.
Source: --url/--key flag → MCPROUTER_URL/MCPROUTER_API_KEY → credentials file.
Store : $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mcprouter/config.json (fallback ~/.config), dir 0700, file 0600,
        written temp+rename. On READ, refuse if the mode is group/world readable.
Exit  : 0 ok · 1 usage/unknown command · 2 API error (body printed) · 3 auth error
Dist  : npm `mcprouter`, engines node>=22. Also baked into the Docker image.
interfaces.notes: Dropped vs mcphub's CLI: config profiles, cache clear, discover, install, export, reinstall, prompts, resources. Install belongs to the UI marketplace — a second implementation of it in the CLI is the definition of unrequested. `doctor` and `secret` are new and exist because our config is strict: if you make configuration fail hard, you owe the operator the tools to satisfy it.

interfaces.name: vitest.config.ts
interfaces.notes: The global numbers are deliberately unambitious so nobody games them; the per-glob numbers are the real gate. Compare mcphub jest.config.cjs:31-38 where all four thresholds are 0.

interfaces.name: gateway.e2e.ts
interfaces.notes: Runs in-process via createApp rather than `docker compose exec` so it is ~90s not ~8min and therefore never gets commented out. A separate release-gated job runs the same assertions against the published image. This whole file is what mcphub lacks: 'no e2e against a built image'.

interfaces.name: Dockerfile
interfaces.sketch:
FROM node:22-bookworm-slim AS base
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git ca-certificates \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.9 /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/
ENV NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/home/node/.cache/npm UV_CACHE_DIR=/home/node/.cache/uv \
    UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/home/node/.local/share/uv/python
RUN su node -c 'uv python install 3.13'     # deterministic uvx, no first-run download, works air-gapped

FROM base AS build
RUN corepack enable
WORKDIR /src
COPY pnpm-lock.yaml pnpm-workspace.yaml package.json ./
COPY packages/*/package.json packages/
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
COPY . .
RUN pnpm build && pnpm deploy --filter @mcprouter/server --prod /out

FROM base AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /out ./
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /src/packages/web/dist ./web
USER node
ENV NODE_ENV=production WEB_DIST=/app/web DATA_DIR=/app/data
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=3s --start-period=20s \
  CMD node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:'+(process.env.PORT||3000)+'/health/live').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1),()=>process.exit(1))"
# no pnpm, no corepack at runtime — corepack re-download breaks non-root / egress-restricted
# runs (mcphub Dockerfile:67-71, a lesson worth copying verbatim)
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
interfaces.notes: One stage set, one variant, amd64+arm64. No entrypoint.sh at all: migrations run in-process under the advisory lock, there is no dockerd to wait for, and npm registry config is plain env. mcphub's entrypoint.sh includes a 15s sleep waiting for dockerd.

interfaces.name: docker-compose.yml
interfaces.sketch:
services:
  db:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16          # EXACT image the integration tests run
    environment: [POSTGRES_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_USER=mcprouter, POSTGRES_DB=mcprouter]
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ./deploy/initdb:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro   # 01-vector.sql: CREATE EXTENSION vector;
    healthcheck: { test: ["CMD-SHELL","pg_isready -U mcprouter"], interval: 5s, retries: 20 }

  app:
    image: ghcr.io/<org>/mcprouter:1
    depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }
    env_file: .env
    ports: ["3000:3000"]
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: [/tmp]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    volumes:
      - data:/app/data                     # MCPB uploads
      - pkgcache:/home/node/.cache         # ONE volume covers npx (_npx) and uvx caches

volumes: { pgdata: {}, data: {}, pkgcache: {} }
interfaces.notes: CREATE EXTENSION runs as the superuser in initdb, so the application role never needs superuser. read_only root fs + explicit writable mounts is the containment boundary for stdio upstreams — spawning arbitrary commands IS the product, so the container, not the app, is the sandbox.

interfaces.name: ci.yml
interfaces.sketch:
on: [pull_request]           # never pull_request_target — PR jobs hold no secrets
permissions: { contents: read }
concurrency: { group: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }

jobs:
  check:        # ~3 min
    - pnpm install --frozen-lockfile        # fails on lockfile drift
    - pnpm lint                              # oxlint + prettier --check
    - pnpm build                             # tsc -b + vite build   ← mcphub has this commented out
    - pnpm test:unit --coverage              # thresholds enforced here
    - pnpm db:generate && git diff --exit-code drizzle/   # schema edited without a migration
  integration:  # ~4 min, needs the runner's docker daemon
    - pnpm test:integration                  # testcontainers pgvector/pgvector:pg16
  e2e:          # ~2 min, timeout-minutes: 8
    - pnpm test:e2e
  image:        # ~3 min
    - docker/build-push-action@<sha>  platforms: linux/amd64  push: false

# CODEOWNERS: /.github/  →  @platform-owners  (disabling a job needs a second approval)
interfaces.notes: Target wall time ≤8 min for the whole PR. Every action pinned to a SHA. Release workflow adds: buildx amd64+arm64 → GHCR with --provenance --sbom, cosign keyless, npm publish --provenance for the CLI, and one e2e run against the pushed image.

interfaces.name: tsconfig topology
interfaces.notes: `references: []` on core is the load-bearing line: core cannot reference server, and pnpm's isolated node_modules means core cannot even resolve `hono` or `better-auth`. That is how 'session identity never enters core' becomes a compile error rather than a code-review convention.

interfaces.name: contracts required from the other seven
interfaces.notes: The one contract I will reject in review: any core export whose parameter list contains a session id, a transport, a Hono Context, or an Mcp-Session-Id. That is the seam the 2026-07-28 migration depends on.

security: Config ingress (env / *_FILE -> process). Secrets arrive only as env vars or files referenced by <VAR>_FILE; validation errors print variable NAMES and never values; the config object carries a non-enumerable toJSON that replaces AUTH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL and EMBEDDING_API_KEY with '[redacted]' so a boot-time logger.info({config}) cannot exfiltrate the database password. .env is in both .gitignore and .dockerignore. AUTH_SECRET has no random fallback (mcphub config/jwt.ts:4-14) and a <32-char value is a hard exit 78.

Identity-origin boundary (PUBLIC_URL). The hub's own identity is taken ONLY from the required PUBLIC_URL, never from the Host or X-Forwarded-Host header. OAuth redirect URIs, the RFC 9728 protected-resource document and the RFC 8707 resource audience all derive from that one constant, so a host-header injection cannot mint a token audience the hub will later accept.

Client-IP boundary (reverse proxy). TRUST_PROXY_HOPS defaults to 0, meaning X-Forwarded-For is ignored and the socket address is used. When set to N, the client IP is the Nth entry from the RIGHT of the XFF chain — the only parse that a client cannot forge by prepending entries. Audit-log source IPs and rate limits both read that one resolved value.

Container boundary (stdio upstreams). Spawning arbitrary commands is the product, so the containment is the container, not the app: non-root USER node, read_only root filesystem with tmpfs /tmp and three explicit writable volumes, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, no Docker-in-Docker (mcphub's INSTALL_EXT ships a dockerd, which is a container escape by design). Children are spawned detached and killed by process group so no orphan npx/uvx survives a restart. STDIO_ENABLED=false lets a paranoid operator remove the surface entirely. Documented plainly: hub-admin is root-equivalent on this container.

Upstream network boundary. UPSTREAM_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS defaults to false and every upstream URL plus every redirect hop is checked against it (mcphub mcpService.ts:1382-1396). Unlike mcphub we do NOT bypass the check for admin-owned servers — that is an implicit ownership rule nobody remembers; ours is one explicit global env that logs a WARN on every boot while it is true.

Database privilege boundary. CREATE EXTENSION vector runs once in docker-entrypoint-initdb.d as the Postgres superuser, so the application role is a plain owner of its schema and never needs superuser. Schema changes can only come from migration files under an advisory lock; there is no synchronize:true path that lets application code alter production DDL (mcphub db/connection.ts:92).

Unauthenticated probe boundary. /health/live and /health/ready return a single status word and nothing else — no version, no migration id, no Postgres error text. Everything an attacker could use for fingerprinting lives behind auth at /api/health. /metrics requires an API key carrying the metrics:read permission (better-auth apiKey `permissions`), because Prometheus series names leak the full upstream server inventory.

CI supply-chain boundary. Workflows trigger on pull_request (never pull_request_target), workflow-level permissions are contents:read, no secret is available to any PR-triggered job, and PR Docker builds never push. Every action is pinned to a commit SHA. Releases add cosign keyless signing, buildx --provenance --sbom and npm publish --provenance. CODEOWNERS on /.github/ means removing a gate needs a second human.

CLI credential boundary. The token file is written temp+rename at 0600 inside a 0700 directory, and is REFUSED on read if its mode is group- or world-readable — mcphub writes 0600 but never verifies on read, so a file that was chmodded or restored from a bad backup is used silently. Flags and env take precedence over the file, so CI never needs to write one.

Dependency boundary. pnpm install --frozen-lockfile on every PR makes a lockfile change a reviewable diff rather than a surprise; pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high runs weekly and on PR; the runtime image contains no compilers, no pnpm and no corepack, so a compromised transitive dep has no build toolchain to reach for.

deferred.item: BASE_PATH plumbing beyond PUBLIC_URL's pathname (for reverse proxies that do not strip the prefix)
deferred.add_when: A user reports the UI 404ing behind a proxy that forwards the full path. Until then vite base:'./' plus app.basePath(new URL(PUBLIC_URL).pathname) covers every proxy that rewrites, which is the default config of nginx, Caddy and Traefik.

deferred.item: Publishing packages/core and packages/server to npm
deferred.add_when: Someone credibly wants to embed the engine in their own Node process, or run the hub without Docker. Today the hard requirement on Postgres 16 + pgvector means npx-without-a-database was never a working path.
There is more than one published package, or more than one release per week. With a single CLI package the git tag is the version and CHANGELOG.md is hand-written in ten lines.

deferred.item: Playwright browser e2e for the SPA
deferred.add_when: The second UI regression that component tests failed to catch. Until then the API e2e covers the contract and the UI is small enough to click through in the PR preview.

A user runs more than one replica. The design is already replica-safe at the data layer (required AUTH_SECRET, advisory-locked migrations, no in-memory config), so this is packaging plus a documented session-affinity annotation — not a redesign.
The QEMU-emulated arm64 release build exceeds 15 minutes. PR builds are amd64-only so this only ever affects the release path.

deferred.item: A separate migration Job/container instead of MIGRATE_ON_BOOT
deferred.add_when: An operator's deployment policy forbids the app role from holding DDL privileges. MIGRATE_ON_BOOT=false plus `node dist/migrate.js` already exists for this; only the packaging is missing.
After 1.0. Before then the dependency set changes faster than a bot could usefully track it.

deferred.item: Windows support for stdio upstreams and the CLI
deferred.add_when: Asked for by a real user. v1 targets Linux containers plus macOS/Linux development; process-group kill semantics differ on Windows and would need a real implementation, not a shim.
The third 'it does not build on my machine'. `docker compose up db` plus node 22 is currently the whole setup.

deferred.item: A `mcprouter install <server>` marketplace command in the CLI
deferred.add_when: Someone needs to provision servers from a script. The UI owns install in P6; a second implementation in the CLI before anyone has asked is the textbook unrequested abstraction.

@modelcontextprotocol/sdk ships LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION='2026-07-28'. Scoped at one week as a sibling file to the legacy handler — the tsconfig reference topology and core's dependency list exist specifically to keep that estimate true.

risks: The e2e job gets slow and someone comments it out — this is precisely how mcphub's build and integration jobs died (ci.yml:48-113). Mitigations: the e2e runs createApp in-process rather than via docker exec so it is ~90s not ~8min; a hard timeout-minutes:8 turns creep into a failure instead of a tax; CODEOWNERS on /.github/ means disabling it needs a second approval.

testcontainers needs a Docker daemon, which CI has but many macOS developers do not (Colima/OrbStack/Docker Desktop are all optional installs). Mitigation: TEST_DATABASE_URL bypasses the container entirely and points at `docker compose up db`, and `pnpm test:unit` alone is a complete pre-commit loop. Risk if unmitigated: integration tests become 'the CI-only tests' and stop being run before push.

tsc project references + verbatimModuleSyntax + mandatory .js extensions in relative ESM imports is real friction for contributors who have only used bundlers. The failure is loud (build error, not runtime), but it will generate 'why does my import not work' issues. Mitigation: one paragraph in CONTRIBUTING and an oxlint rule pointing at the fix.

Baking a uv-managed CPython at image build time pins us to whatever uv resolves that day, so two builds of the same git SHA weeks apart can differ. Accepted deliberately — the alternative (downloading a Python at container start) fails in air-gapped and egress-restricted deploys, which is a worse failure. Mitigation: pin the uv image minor and the Python version string; revisit if reproducible builds become a requirement.

The per-glob 90% coverage gates on security modules can be gamed by tests that import broadly without asserting. Coverage measures execution, not verification. Mitigation: those globs are also the ones where a human reviewer is required, and the e2e asserts the actual invariant (hidden error === missing error) independently of any coverage number.

EMBEDDING_DIM is fixed by a migration, so changing the embedding model to one with a different dimension is a schema change, not a config change. assertEmbeddingDim fails loudly at boot with the remedy in the message, but an operator who expected to swap models by editing .env will be annoyed. Documented in .env.example next to the variable.

Requiring AUTH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL and PUBLIC_URL with no defaults means the very first `docker compose up` fails unless .env was filled in. That is a worse thirty-second experience than mcphub's silent random secret, in exchange for never debugging intermittent token rejection across replicas. Mitigation: compose ships an .env.example the quickstart copies in one command, and `mcprouter secret` generates the value.

Single Docker image with no INSTALL_EXT variant means any upstream MCP server that needs a runtime we do not ship (Rust, Java, Go, a browser) simply cannot run in-container. This is a real capability loss versus mcphub's latest-full. Mitigation and documented answer: run those as sibling containers and register them as streamable-http upstreams — which is also the safer architecture. Risk accepted; revisit if more than two users hit it.

v1 serves the legacy era, so downstream session state is in packages/server memory and multi-replica needs session affinity on /mcp. If an operator load-balances round-robin without reading the README, they get intermittent 'unknown session' errors. Mitigation: the README states it, and /api/health reports the replica id so the symptom is diagnosable in one request. The 2026-07-28 spec deletes the requirement outright.
